raw_response:
I have been farming this same land in Quzhou for over sixty years. I know this soil. My back is not what it was, and I cannot do the heavy work myself anymore — my son helps when he can, and I hire a neighbor's machine for planting and harvest. But I still make the decisions.

Here, everyone grows wheat then corn on the same fields. That is what I will do again. I know no other way, and at my age I have no reason to change. I will farm my 4 mu, the same as last year.

For the wheat I plant in October — I use an improved variety the seed shop sells, the same kind I have used for several years. It does well here. I will put down base fertilizer before planting and top-dress at jointing. We need to irrigate — this county has no reliable rain. I pump from the groundwater well four times over the winter and spring: once before freeze, once at jointing, once at heading, once at grain fill. I spray for aphids and mildew twice. I use the rotary tiller before seeding because the soil needs to be loose.

After wheat harvest in June I plant corn immediately on the same land. Hybrid seed — that is all the shop sells anymore and the yield is better. I irrigate twice if no rain comes. One pesticide spray for stem borer. No tilling — I just plant into the stubble.

I expect about 450 jin of wheat and 550 jin of corn per mu. Enough to sell some and keep some.
